If that ruling changes the sub-choice rule, THIS ITEM IS REVISITED THEN. Recorded the same way the temporal_composition instances were: provisional and findable, not silently settled.

IT IS AN OBLIGATION, and §2.5 does not exclude it. It commands conduct (dispute only in good faith) and 'reasonable good faith' is a REVIEWABLE standard -- §2.5.1's own discriminator, the thing that separates an eligible clause from 'sole business judgment'. Breachable and monitorable.

ACTION: A GENUINE GAP WITH NO NEAR MEMBER. DISPUTE, CHALLENGE, OBJECT and CONTEST are all absent from the real 34-verb ACTIONS, verified by execution. The full 34-verb pass C10-02's notes establish as the procedure was run, and unlike C10-02 ('add' -> ESTABLISH) or C14-04 ('perform ... to complete' -> PROCESS) NOTHING IS SEMANTICALLY ADJACENT. Three candidates were weighed and are recorded rather than dropped: PROCESS (C14-04's generic-but-honest fallback -- honest about the poor fit, conveys nothing about the clause); COMPLY (reads the duty as 'conform your disputing to a standard'); NEGOTIATE (a disputed invoice opens a resolution process, but the duty is not to negotiate). PROCESS taken on C14-04's precedent that a generic honest verb beats a wrong specific one. Single-member accept-set per §8.8's genuine-gap branch; NO widening, which is the very rule the §10 question below is about.

OBJECT_CLASS: THE SLOT DELIBERATELY AVOIDS RESTATING THE REAL VERB, AND THE SET DELIBERATELY KEEPS IT. §3.6.1's own Standing-Principle-7 note records that its screen 'is blind to any item carrying an action_not_in_taxonomy tag, where the label may restate the REAL verb while action holds a different one' -- C10-02's '_listing' against the real verb 'add' is the worked miss, and this item is exactly that shape. 'disputed_amounts' would restate the real verb 'dispute'. Strictly §3.6.1 is content-relative to THIS item's field values (action = PROCESS) so it is not violated, but the section's own instruction is to re-run it BY HAND against §8.8 items rather than trust the screen. Done here: the SLOT is the bare head noun 'amounts', which restates nothing, while 'disputed_amounts' is RETAINED AS A MEMBER -- §3.6.1's set rule is widening-only and a member is never removed, and it is a faithful reading of the object. That is §3.6.1's slot/set asymmetry applied deliberately rather than discovered later.

CONDITIONS EMPTY. 'in reasonable good faith' is a reviewable-standard phrase and is NOT a conditions entry (§3.8, v0.54, first instance C04-06) -- it governs HOW the right is exercised, not WHETHER the duty applies. This is the second locked instance of that rule and the first where the same phrase is simultaneously load-bearing for §2.5.1 eligibility, which §3.8 says in terms is the point rather than a tension.

MODALITY MUST. 'shall only dispute' is a restrictive positive, not a negative; §3.2 maps 'shall' to MUST and §3.3 forbids an accept-set. MUST_NOT was considered ('shall not dispute other than in good faith') and rejected as a paraphrase the text does not use.

OBLIGEE ABSENT -- NFI is not inside this span (it first occurs at 'provide NFI', outside [81:144]) and §3.5 forbids inferring a party from elsewhere. §8.4.2 does not fire: (b) fails on a single named obligor.
segment_text: KIRKLAND’S shall pay all undisputed amounts invoiced as provided in Section 6.2. KIRKLAND’S shall only dispute amounts in reasonable good faith and shall provide NFI with written notice of the basis for disputing any amounts on an invoice within 30 days of KIRKLAND’S’s receipt of NFI’s invoice. Payments not received by NFI within fifteen (15) days of KIRKLAND’S’s receipt of written notice that such payment is overdue will be subject to a service charge of 1% per month on the unpaid balance.
